Local anaesthetic agents administered topically to skin or mucosa include:

- Lignocaine gels and spray formulations
- EMLA: eutectic mixture of local anaesthetics, contains lignocaine and prilocaine 
- Amethocaine for skin or eye anaesthesia 
- Cocaine

Toxicity = unwanted harmful effect of a drug

Toxicity from LAs can be classified into local or systemic effects

**Toxicity can include:**

- Hypersensitivity reaction
- Skin / mucosa irritation
- Systemic Toxicity 
- Methemoglobinemia

**Hypersensitivity Reaction:**

LA can cause allergy/hypersensitivity reactions → easter LA \> Amide LA 

**Agent Specific:**

Prilocaine → Methaemoglobin 

Cocaine → ↑SNS ( ↑SVT/CO/mAP)  and CNS effects euphoria etc

**LA Systemic Toxicity (LAST):**

Dose related effect with circumoral numbness/tingling → dysarthria → Visual changes → seizures → LOC → respiratory depression → CVS depression 

CVS Toxicity: 

Vasodilatation at low concentrations, vasoconstriction at high concentrations. 

Inhibition of cardiac Na+ channels, inhibiting maximum rate of rise of phase 0 of the cardiac action potential.

 Negative inotropy proportional to potency

CNS Toxicity:

Does-dependent CNS effects: circumoral tingling, visual disturbances, tinnitus, tremors, dizziness, slurred speech, convulsions, coma, apnoea. 

Potentiated by other CNS depressants and hypercarbia (due to ↑ CBF and ↓ seizure threshold

**Factors Affecting LAST:**

Systemic Absorption of local anaesthetics applied to skin or mucosa are governed by Fick’s law of diffusion.

Diffusion = (ΔPxAxk)/t

ΔP = concentration gradient. ↑dose / concentration of agent applied →↑ rate of diffusion →↑ risk of toxicity 

A = Area of diffusion. Larger diffusion area → more rapid diffusion →↑risk of toxicity

k = diffusion constant given by solubility / sq(MW). ↑LA solubility/lipophilicity or smaller molecule size → more rapid absorption

Thickness of membrane: LA applied to thick skin will diffuse more slowly while thin skin or mucosa will result in rapid diffusion  

Other factors that affect the rate of systemic absorption include local blood flow/vascularity of site. ↑vascularity → increased/more rapid systemic spread →↑ risk of LAST 

**Pharmacokinetics (PK):**

> - Esters: rapid metabolism by BChE → short t~1/2β~
> - Amides: slow metabolism by liver → long t~1/2β~

**Pharmacodynamics (PD):**

> - Toxicity threshold: bupivacaine 1.5mcg/mL, ropivacaine 4mcg/mL, lignocaine 5mcg/mL
> - CC:CNS ratio – bupivacaine 3:1, ropivacaine 5:1, lignocaine 7:1
